items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: But it was much more four beat and it was much more like Condon’s stuff.

ctx.x: Yes it’s hard to label things.

But I mean the real, as you can imagine, with Jimmy Wormworth on drums it was basically a bop drummer, we were a four beat Dixieland band, which is sort of interesting because we didn’t have a bass most of the time, we had a banjo. So it was kind of a unique mix to have the standard front line of trumpet, clarinet and trombone, but then sort of this mixed up rhythm section of a bop drummer, a really sort of classical or outstanding cocktail pianist piano player and a banjo player. But it worked fine. But I think…
So the group didn’t really think of itself as playing — I’m not sure how to put this — but old music.
